_about: Banks for the auction house generator. Auction houses are found only in settlements with 'auction' set in items.json. Estimates are in gp and shown in spirit coins (1 iron = 1 gp, 1 bronze = 100 gp, 1 silver = 10,000 gp). 'stock' sets what each settlement's auctions offer: magic item rarities, essence rarities, awakening stone levels, core ranks and how many lots. 'exotica' are one-of-a-kind lots of the world's own. Edit freely; {place}, {faction}, {npc} and {church} are filled from your wiki.
looks: Rows of velvet chairs face a raised stage where each lot is carried out on a cushion by gloved porters.
A domed hall of white stone, with private boxes on a gallery for buyers who would rather not be seen bidding.
A converted warehouse by the docks, smelling of tar and money, with lots displayed in iron cages before the sale.
A hushed gallery where every lot sits behind glass for a week before the sale, guarded by Bronze-rankers who never smile.
An old temple bought by a merchant house, the altar now the auctioneer's podium and the pews full of bidders.
A sale held on a barge moored in the harbour, so that no city ward has any say over what is sold.
A converted chapel with pews for bidders and lots displayed on the altar.
An open courtyard with a canvas roof, lots shown on carts wheeled through the crowd.
A cellar under a bank, lit by candles, where only invited bidders may enter.
A grand ballroom with chandeliers, the lots shown on a rotating stage.
A ship's hold, moored in the harbour, so the house can sail if the law comes.
A garden pavilion where bidders sit at tables and servants bring wine between lots.
auctioneerStyles: Talks so fast that newcomers miss their chance; regulars love it.
Slow, dry and theatrical, pausing so long before the hammer that people bid out of nerves.
Remembers every bidder's name and uses it, which makes it very hard to stop bidding.
Tells a short, possibly true story about each lot before opening it.
Never raises their voice and never needs to; the room goes silent when they lift the gavel.
Jokes with the crowd, flatters the rich and teases the cautious into one more bid.
Sings every bid, which is charming for one lot and maddening by the tenth.
A Runic woman whose marks glow brighter as the price climbs.
Insults low bidders by name, and the crowd loves it.
Speaks only in whispers, so the whole room leans in.
Tells a little story about each lot before the bidding, some of it true.
A retired adventurer who handles each weapon and armour piece as if testing it.
rules: Bids are called in spirit coins. The hammer is final.
Every lot may be inspected the day before the sale. The house makes no promises beyond its written appraisal.
Payment is due by sundown on the day of sale; unpaid lots go back on the block and the bidder is banned.
Proxy bids may be left in a sealed letter with the clerk.
Fighting, spellcasting and the use of essence abilities in the hall are forbidden. The guards are Bronze rank.
A paddle is issued to each registered bidder for a deposit of 1 bronze spirit coin, returned at the end.
Sellers may set a hidden reserve; a lot that fails to reach it is withdrawn without comment.
Bidders may stay anonymous through a house agent, for a fee.
Buyers may send a proxy, who must carry a sealed letter of authority.
Any lot may be withdrawn by the seller up to the moment of the first bid.
Fighting in the hall bans the fighter and their whole team for life.
The house holds each lot for three days after sale; uncollected lots are resold.
No one may bid on their own consigned lots, and the house checks.
Lots of essence are sold only to those who show an Adventure Society badge or a noble seal.
provenance: Recovered from an astral space by a Bronze-rank team who need the coins more than the item.
From the estate of a minor noble house, sold to cover gambling debts.
Seized by the Adventure Society from a cult's hideout and sold by order of the Society.
Consigned by {faction}, who will not say how they came by it.
Found in a monster's hoard after a surge was put down near {place}.
Brought in by a ship's captain from across the sea, with a story that changes each time it is told.
The last piece of a famous adventurer's collection, sold by grandchildren who never met them.
Comes with a sealed Magic Society appraisal, signed by three scholars.
Consigned anonymously through a house agent. The clerk will only say the seller is 'from out of town'.
Recovered from a wrecked caravan on the road; the house says the owners are 'presumed dead'.
Sold by {npc}, who needs money quickly and won't say why.
Said to have belonged to a priest of {church}, though the church has made no claim.
Found in the hold of a ship that came back with no crew.
Recovered from a monster's nest, where it had been for decades.
Sold by a Gold-rank adventurer retiring to the country.
Part of a dowry returned after a broken engagement.
Brought by a Storm Kingdom trader, with papers no one here can check.
Dug up by a farmer ploughing a new field.
Taken from a cult's shrine by the Church of Justice and sold to fund its work.
From the collection of a Magic Society scholar who died without heirs.
Won in a card game by the current seller, who'd rather have coin.
Smuggled out of a war zone across the sea.
From the vault of a noble house that fell from favour.
Recovered by divers from a sunken city off the coast.
rivals: a veiled agent of {faction}, who bids by lifting one finger
a young noble spending their family's money far too fast
a Silver-rank adventurer who looks bored until the right lot comes up
a Magic Society scholar with a strict budget and a list
a merchant from across the sea who bids in round numbers only
a house agent bidding for someone who isn't in the room
a retired adventurer who wants back something they lost long ago
a priest of {church}, bidding on behalf of the temple
a collector who buys anything with a good story
a nervous clerk from {faction}, clearly told not to come back without it
a pair of Bronze-rank siblings pooling their coins and arguing in whispers
an elderly elf who never bids before the hammer is about to fall
an old woman in a shawl who bids huge sums and pays in gold bars
a Magic Society buyer with a list and a strict budget
a merchant from the steppes who bids by raising a horsewhip
a pair of twins bidding against each other, apparently by accident
a church treasurer who keeps praying before each bid
a masked buyer whose servant does all the talking
a drunk heir who bids on everything and pays for nothing
a Silver-rank team pooling their coins and arguing at each raise
an outworlder collector who wants anything from another world
a famous chef bidding on monster ingredients
a quiet Leonid who never bids until the hammer is about to fall
an agent of the duke, whose bids no one dares to top
events: Halfway through, a lot is withdrawn when someone stands and shouts that it was stolen from them.
A bidding war between two rivals turns personal, and the auctioneer has to call the guards.
One lot reacts to someone in the room: it glows, hums or grows cold as they pass.
The lights go out for a moment, and when they return the auctioneer counts the lots twice.
A latecomer sweeps in, bids on one lot only, and leaves without a word.
An outworlder in the crowd laughs out loud at a lot, then refuses to explain.
A Society inspector arrives and asks to see the paperwork for one lot.
The house adds a surprise lot at the end that isn't in the catalogue.
A bidder faints when the price passes what they can pay.
The lights go out for a few seconds; when they return, a lot is gone.
The auctioneer is bribed, mid-sale, in plain sight.
A lot turns out to be a monster in disguise, and the sale stops.
A noble accuses another of bidding with stolen money.
The house reveals a surprise lot, not in the catalogue.
A bidder's servant switches sides and bids against them.
The watch arrives with a warrant for one lot.
A lot speaks, and the auctioneer pretends it didn't.
The seller tries to buy their own item back.
A small fire starts in the storeroom and smoke fills the hall.
Someone pays for their lot with a cursed coin.
secrets: One of the rivals is a shill paid by the house to push the prices up. They stop at once if bid against hard.
{npc} has arranged to buy the best lot whatever it costs, and will be very unhappy with whoever outbids them.
A thief plans to steal one lot from the winner on their way home tonight.
The auctioneer owes money to {faction} and is quietly steering one lot their way.
One lot was stolen from {place} last year, and its owner is in the room.
The house appraiser was bribed to overstate one lot's powers.
A rival bidder is an agent of a foreign crown, buying anything that could help an army.
The sale is being watched by {faction}, who are noting who buys what.
The best lot is a forgery, and the house knows.
The auctioneer is selling information about bidders to a crime boss.
One lot is wanted by a cult that will kill to get it.
The house is going bankrupt and this sale is its last chance.
A seller has consigned an item that belongs to the duke.
One of the porters is a thief who swaps lots for fakes.
The house's appraiser can't tell real essences from fakes and is too proud to admit it.
A buyer is an assassin, here to find their target, not to bid.
A lot contains a hidden map, sewn into its lining.
The seller of the top lot is dead, and the person who consigned it killed them.
Two rival houses have both promised the same lot to their patrons.
The house deliberately undervalues lots from poor sellers and resells them at a profit.
exotica: A sealed Bronze-rank monster egg, warm to the touch
Hatches within a season if kept warm. What hatches imprints on the first person it sees, and it grows quickly.
A map to an unopened astral space
Hand-drawn by the last surviving member of the team that found it. The space has not yet been claimed by the Adventure Society.
The skull of a Gold-rank monster
Huge, polished and still faintly radiating magic. Alchemists and crafters prize the bone.
A Silver-rank monster core, still pulsing
A single core of extraordinary purity. Enough to train a Silver-ranker for weeks, or power a city ward for a year.
A shard of a broken god's statue
Cold, heavy and impossible to scratch. DM: it whispers at night to whoever holds it.
An outworlder's belongings
Strange clothes, a flat glass slab that does nothing, and a book in an unknown script. The seller swears they came from another world.
A cloud-flask that unfolds into a cottage
Shaped cloud that becomes a small house with doors, rooms and a working hearth, for as long as it is needed.
A ship's figurehead carved from a living tree
It still grows leaves in spring, and sailors say a ship that carries it never sinks.
Scales of a Silver-rank sea serpent (a full set)
Enough for one suit of the finest scale armour, if a Silver-rank crafter can be found to work it.
A sealed letter from a dead queen
Never opened. The seal is still warded. Historians and at least one noble house want it badly.
A bottle of essence-grade wine, two centuries old
Brewed with monster fruit. A single glass restores an essence user as fully as a long rest.
A cage holding a live Iron-rank monster cub
Fierce, hungry and young enough to be raised. The Adventure Society has not been told.
The badge of a famous adventurer, Gold rank
A Gold-rank Adventure Society badge from a hero who died a generation ago. Not a working badge, but priceless to collectors.
A pristine awakening stone of unknown affinity
No appraiser can name the essence it would awaken. It hums in a chord no one recognises.
A jar of shadow that never empties, however much is poured out
Pours like ink and evaporates in sunlight. Useful for covering tracks, or a dark room.
A Silver-rank monster's skull, polished and set with a candle holder
The candle burns without smoke and never melts down. The skull's jaw moves when anyone lies near it.
A compass that points to the nearest astral space
Spins wildly in cities. In the wild it is uncannily accurate.
A cloak woven from a giant spider's silk
Weighs almost nothing, turns blades poorly and climbs walls well; the wearer feels very slightly hungry for flies.
A music box that plays a different song for every listener
Each listener hears the song they most need to hear. Nobody agrees on what it played.
A sealed letter from a dead king, never opened
Its seal is intact, and the Magic Society says it is magically warded. Everyone wants to know what it says.
A feather from a phoenix-touched bird, still warm
Warm forever. Placed on a corpse within a minute of death, it may buy a breath. May.
A set of dice carved from a monster's teeth
Roll true for honest gamblers. Roll badly for cheats, with surprising accuracy.
A chessboard where the pieces move themselves at night
Plays a single, very slow game against whoever owns it. It's winning.
A bottle of seawater from the far side of the world
Smells of a different ocean. Merfolk pay well for a single drop.
